Subject: Initial MAP + evidence ask for procurement sequencing

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at CardinalRX is excited about Redwood's latency profile and routing fallback options. Procurement has asked me to put together a mutual action plan (MAP) that clearly sequences the MSA, DPA and order form milestones alongside the evaluation gates so we can commit resources on our side.

Two specific asks from procurement/legal:
- Can we get a staged MAP that shows which signatures and evidence items (SOC 2 cert, data retention policy, audit logging screenshots) are required to reach each milestone (pilot, production pilot, GA)?
- Cardinal needs the order form to be able to follow the DPA signature but they prefer a hard dependency that prevents billing before DPA is in place.

I've attached a simple template (Cardinal_MAP_v2.xlsx) with suggested milestones — feel free to edit. Can you confirm Redwood's preferred gating for order forms vs DPA? Also: target timeline is 8–10 weeks from pilot kickoff.

Best,
Sam

Subject: Re: Initial MAP + evidence ask for procurement sequencing

Hi Sam — thanks for sending the template and for the clear asks. We're aligned on the high-level approach; below is how Redwood typically sequences these items and a proposed two-track MAP to minimize blocker risk.

Quick summary (proposed):
1) Pilot kickoff (Week 0): SOW + pilot order form signed — billing capped at pilot usage; pilot payables held in escrow / nominal charge.
2) Evidence collection window (Weeks 1–3): Redwood provides SOC 2 attestation excerpt, data retention summary, and a short screencap walkthrough of audit logs.
3) DPA signature (Week 3–4 preferred): DPA executed before production order form is unblocked. We can accept an electronic signature; legal asks a short negotiated clause set (we can surface a one-page redline).
4) Production order form transition (Week 4–6): Order form moves from pilot to production billing once DPA is effective. If procurement needs the order form earlier for internal approvals, we can deliver a draft that is explicitly conditioned on DPA execution (no billing).
5) GA readiness (Week 8–10): Final acceptance criteria & go-live.

Key notes / risks:
- If Cardinal requires a locked order form that automatically invoices regardless of DPA state, that creates legal risk and we will request an escrow/credit hold.
- For evidence, SOC 2 excerpt + Evidence_Index.pdf is low friction; anything requiring an on-site audit will push the timeline.

I'm attaching a lightly annotated MAP back to your template with our gating suggestions. Laura from legal has visibility — Laura, can you confirm the DPA redline lead time and whether Redwood can accept conditioned order forms that explicitly state \"no billing until DPA executed\"?

Thanks — I'll hold a 30-minute call Mon morning if useful.

Cheers,
Jonas

Attachments: Cardinal_MAP_v2_annotated.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial MAP + evidence ask for procurement sequencing

Hi all — adding legal context and a recommended gating pattern.

Short answer: Yes, we can accept a conditioned order form that contains explicit language preventing billing until the DPA is fully executed. Recommended phrasing we typically use (we can provide exact text):
- \"This Order Form is executed subject to the Parties completing the Data Processing Addendum. No charges shall be invoiced or payable under this Order Form until the DPA is fully executed; notwithstanding, the Parties may sign this Order Form in advance for procurement approval purposes.\"

Operational points:
- DPA lead time for a one-page redline turnaround: 48–72 hours once procurement/legal provides counterpoints. Complex redlines (data residency, archiving windows, vendor subprocessors) will add ~1 week.
- Evidence bundle: we will provide SOC 2 type II excerpt, data retention spec, audit log screenshots and a small runbook for evidence ingestion. Evidence_Index.pdf attached.
- For invoice gating we prefer the conditioned order form + internal finance ticket to avoid manual credit holds. If Cardinal requires automatic invoicing, we'll need an approved credit hold process.

Rishi / Grace — please note: if procurement requests DPA exceptions for \"de-identified analytics\" we need a separate data flow appendix; that will be an additional week.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
